gloss: lower level; bottom tier; low guard

definitions.gloss: lower level; bottom tier; lower shelf
definitions.explanation: The lower section of a shelf, display, rack, or other vertically divided structure. Used for furniture, storage, and page layouts.
In martial arts (especially kendo, judo, and karate), a defensive position where the weapon or body is held low. One of the five basic guard positions in kendo.

examples.japanese: {下段|げだん}の{棚|たな}に{置|お}いてある。
{冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}の{下段|げだん}に{野菜|やさい}を{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I put the vegetables on the bottom shelf of the refrigerator.

examples.japanese: ページの{下段|げだん}に{注釈|ちゅうしゃく}が{記載|きさい}されている。
examples.english: Notes are listed in the lower section of the page.
He took a low guard stance.

examples.japanese: {剣道|けんどう}の{基本|きほん}の{構|かま}えには{上段|じょうだん}と{中段|ちゅうだん}と{下段|げだん}がある。
examples.english: The basic stances in kendo include the high guard, middle guard, and low guard.

examples.japanese: {相手|あいて}が{上段|じょうだん}に{構|かま}えたので、こちらは{下段|げだん}で{迎|むか}え{撃|う}った。
examples.english: Since the opponent took a high guard, I countered with a low guard.

notes:
Composed of {下|げ} (lower) and {段|だん} (step, tier, level). Part of a spatial set with {上段|じょうだん} (upper level) and {中段|ちゅうだん} (middle level). The everyday sense (lower shelf/section) is straightforward, but the martial arts sense is culturally significant — {下段|げだん}の{構|かま}え is one of the five classical guard positions in kendo.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {下段|げだん}の{棚|たな}: lower shelf
- {下段|げだん}に{置|お}く: to place on the lower level
- {下段|げだん}の{構|かま}え: low guard stance
- {下段|げだん}に{構|かま}える: to take a low guard
- {下段|げだん}{蹴|げ}り: low kick (in karate)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {上段|じょうだん}: upper level; high guard — the opposite position
- {中段|ちゅうだん}: middle level; middle guard — the neutral position
- {下|した}: bottom, below — more general and informal
